questions.prompt: Why is blocking on an async `Task` with `.Result` or `.Wait()` dangerous in ASP.NET / UI apps?

options.text: It risks thread-pool starvation and deadlocks if the continuation needs the blocked synchronization context or thread

questions.prompt: Why should `async void` methods be avoided except for top-level UI/event handlers?

options.text: Callers cannot `await` them, and unhandled exceptions crash the entire process instead of being captured on a `Task`

questions.prompt: When is `ConfigureAwait(false)` recommended in general-purpose .NET library code?

options.text: When library code doesn't need to resume on the caller's original `SynchronizationContext` (avoiding context-switch overhead and UI deadlocks)

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `ValueTask<T>` vs `Task<T>`. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A `ValueTask<T>` MUST only be `await`ed once and never awaited concurrently or `.Result`ed while incomplete
Default to `Task<T>` for general APIs unless profiling shows `Task` allocation pressure
You can `await` the same `ValueTask<T>` instance multiple times safely
`ValueTask<T>` avoids allocating a heap `Task<T>` object when the method frequently completes synchronously (e.g., cache hit)

questions.prompt: Match each ASP.NET Core Dependency Injection lifetime to its scope.

columns.label: New instance created every time it is requested
One instance per HTTP request / DI scope
Single shared instance for the entire application lifetime

questions.prompt: What is a 'captive dependency' bug in .NET Dependency Injection?

options.text: Injecting a `Scoped` service (like EF Core `DbContext`) into a `Singleton` service—causing the scoped service to live forever and break concurrency

questions.prompt: Why should `CancellationToken` be passed through async I/O and DB calls?

options.text: So aborted HTTP requests or shutdown signals cancel in-flight work promptly instead of wasting server CPU/DB connections

questions.prompt: What does `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` + `await foreach` enable?

options.text: Asynchronous streaming of items as they arrive (e.g., paginated APIs, DB cursors, gRPC streams) without buffering all items in RAM

questions.prompt: Why can't you use `await` inside a `lock (syncObj) { ... }` block in C#?

options.text: Thread-affine `Monitor` locks cannot be released on a different thread after `await`; use `SemaphoreSlim(1, 1).WaitAsync(ct)` instead

questions.prompt: What does `System.Threading.Channels.Channel<T>` provide for producer-consumer pipelines?

options.text: A lock-free/async-friendly bounded or unbounded queue supporting `await writer.WriteAsync` and `await foreach` consumption

questions.prompt: What is the Large Object Heap (LOH) in .NET GC, and what threshold places an object on it?

options.text: Objects >= 85,000 bytes (~85 KB) go to LOH (collected with Gen 2, historically uncompacted by default), so pool large buffers via `ArrayPool<byte>.Shared`

questions.prompt: What does `Memory<T>` solve that `Span<T>` cannot?

options.text: `Memory<T>` is a normal struct (not `ref struct`) so it can be stored in fields and used across `await` boundaries, calling `.Span` synchronously inside helpers

questions.prompt: What subtle pitfall exists with `ConcurrentDictionary<K, V>.GetOrAdd(key, valueFactory)`?

options.text: `valueFactory` may execute multiple times concurrently if two threads miss at once (only one winner is stored)—wrap in `Lazy<T>` if single initialization is required
It locks the whole dictionary on reads

questions.prompt: Select all .NET features/practices that enable NativeAOT and fast startup without reflection overhead. (Select all that apply.)
Why is `[LoggerMessage]` or message-template logging (`logger.LogInformation("Order {OrderId} failed", id)`) better than `logger.LogInformation($"Order {id} failed")`?

options.text: Structured logging preserves `OrderId` as a queryable property AND skips string formatting completely if the log level is disabled

questions.prompt: What does `Task.WhenAll(t1, t2)` do compared to `await t1; await t2;`?

options.text: Awaits both tasks concurrently and completes when all finish (note: `await Task.WhenAll` unwraps the first exception; inspect `task.Exception` for all)

questions.prompt: What is `PeriodicTimer` (.NET 6+) preferred over `System.Timers.Timer` for in `BackgroundService` loops?

options.text: Async-first (`await timer.WaitForNextTickAsync(ct)`), avoids overlapping callback reentrancy, and doesn't root callbacks

questions.prompt: What does `TimeProvider` (.NET 8+) solve for unit testing time-dependent services?

options.text: Abstracts `GetUtcNow()` and `CreateTimer` so tests can inject `FakeTimeProvider` and advance time deterministically without `Task.Delay` flakiness

questions.prompt: What does `stackalloc byte[256]` into a `Span<byte>` do?

options.text: Allocates 256 bytes directly on the current stack frame with zero GC pressure (keep small, e.g. <= 1 KB, and never inside loops!)

questions.prompt: Match each .NET concurrency/memory tool to its ideal use case.

columns.label: Renting and returning temporary large buffers without GC/LOH churn
Async-safe mutual exclusion or concurrency throttling

questions.prompt: What does `Interlocked.Increment(ref _count)` guarantee?

options.text: Performs a lock-free atomic CPU increment across threads without a mutex

questions.prompt: What is the danger of `Task.Run(() => ...)` inside an ASP.NET Core request handler?

options.text: Offloading work to another thread-pool thread just steals a thread from the same ASP.NET thread pool, adding context-switch overhead without adding concurrency

questions.prompt: What does `[GeneratedRegex("^\\d+$")]` (.NET 7+) improve over `new Regex(...)`?

options.text: Generates specialized C# matching code at compile time with zero startup regex-compilation cost and NativeAOT support

questions.prompt: What does `RegexOptions.NonBacktracking` (.NET 7+) prevent?

options.text: Catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS) denial-of-service on adversarial inputs by guaranteeing linear-time matching

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about Garbage Collection (GC) generations in .NET. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Calling `GC.Collect()` in every request handler improves web throughput
Gen 0 holds newly allocated short-lived objects and is collected most frequently and fastest
Objects surviving Gen 0 promote to Gen 1, then Gen 2 (long-lived objects)
Finalizers (`~MyClass()`) delay collection by at least one extra GC cycle—avoid finalizers unless owning raw unmanaged handles directly (prefer `SafeHandle`)

questions.prompt: What does `SafeHandle` provide over raw `IntPtr` + custom finalizer `~Wrapper()`?

options.text: Reliable critical-finalization and reference-counting protection against handle recycling and thread aborts for OS handles

questions.prompt: What does `frozen` collections (`FrozenDictionary` / `FrozenSet` in .NET 8+) optimize?

options.text: Read-heavy lookup tables initialized once at startup (e.g., routing/config maps) with faster lookups than `Dictionary`

questions.prompt: What does `SearchValues<char>` (.NET 8+) optimize?

options.text: SIMD-accelerated searching (`IndexOfAny`) for fixed sets of characters or bytes

questions.prompt: What does `StringSyntaxAttribute` (`[StringSyntax(StringSyntaxAttribute.Json)]`) do?

options.text: Provides IDE syntax highlighting and diagnostics for string parameters containing JSON, Regex, SQL, or URIs

questions.prompt: What is a common memory leak source in long-lived C# services?

options.text: Subscribing to events (`publisher.OnEvent += handler`) on a long-lived publisher without unsubscribing (`-=`) when short-lived subscribers finish

questions.prompt: What does `ActivitySource` + `Meter` (`System.Diagnostics`) provide in modern .NET?

options.text: Native OpenTelemetry-compatible distributed tracing (spans) and metrics with zero external SDK lock-in

questions.prompt: What does `dotnet-counters` / `dotnet-dump` / `dotnet-trace` diagnose in production?

options.text: Live GC heap/gen stats, thread-pool starvation, CPU flamegraphs, and memory dump leaks on running .NET processes

questions.prompt: Match each .NET performance/safety analyzer or pattern to its target bug.

columns.label: Replaces `lock` when `await` is needed inside critical section

questions.prompt: What does `builder.Host.UseDefaultServiceProvider(o => o.ValidateOnBuild = true)` catch at startup?

options.text: Missing DI registrations and captive-dependency scope errors immediately on app boot rather than at first request

questions.prompt: What does `sealed` + `internal` + Roslyn analyzers (`<AnalysisLevel>latest</AnalysisLevel>`) enforce?

options.text: Compile-time code quality, nullability, disposal (`CA2000`), and performance rules across CI builds

questions.prompt: What does `Unbounded` vs `Bounded` `Channel` change under heavy producer load?

options.text: Unbounded channels can grow RAM until OOM if consumers fall behind; Bounded channels apply backpressure (`WaitToWriteAsync` or drop policies)

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `Record` equality vs `Class` equality in C#. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Two `record` instances with identical properties and a `List<int>` field compare the `List<int>` by *reference* (not list contents!)
`class` defaults to reference equality (same object in memory)
`record` generates structural value equality comparing all properties

questions.prompt: What does `MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)` hint to the RyuJIT compiler?

options.text: Encourages inlining a small hot method across calls (use sparingly—JIT already inlines small methods automatically)

questions.prompt: What does `CollectionsMarshal.AsSpan(list)` allow (and what is its strict safety rule)?

options.text: Zero-copy `Span<T>` access to a `List<T>`'s internal array—NEVER add/remove/resize `list` while the `Span` is in use!

questions.prompt: What does `CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(ct1, ct2)` do?

options.text: Creates a token that cancels automatically as soon as *either* `ct1` or `ct2` cancels (remember to `using` dispose it!)

questions.prompt: Select all valid ways to avoid `NullReferenceException` and fragile error handling in C#. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Use `TryParse` / `TryGetValue` / Result patterns for expected failures instead of throwing exceptions in control flow
Wrap the entire application in `catch (Exception) { }` and ignore errors

questions.prompt: Why does `IAsyncDisposable` exist alongside `IDisposable`?

options.text: So types that flush network/file buffers asynchronously during cleanup (like `StreamWriter`, `DbTransaction`, `Utf8JsonWriter`) don't have to block a thread in `Dispose()`
